key_insight: An eigenvalue-based neural constitutive model jointly learns yield behavior and evolution laws for isotropic elastoplasticity while enforcing thermodynamic consistency, including non-associative flow.
engineering_relevance: The approach enables flexible, data-driven plasticity models to be integrated into finite element simulations of boundary-value problems.
method: Use permutation-invariant spectral representations to enforce isotropy and convexity across learnable components.
Construct the non-associative yield function by adding a jointly learned term to a convex flow potential.
Train through a backward-Euler return map using implicit differentiation and eigenvalue-degeneracy-aware gradients.
evidence_signal: Evaluation includes reproducing known constitutive models, learning from full-field finite element stress–strain data and homogenized foam RVEs, and deployment in plane-stress finite element simulations.
watch_item: Implementation requires careful handling of implicit return-map differentiation near repeated eigenvalues; the stated scope is rate-independent, isotropic elastoplasticity.
paper_title: Thermodynamically consistent neural constitutive models for elastoplasticity via eigen-representations
